clusters.name: Diligence and Work Ethic
clusters.description: The ant as a model of self-motivated industry and the consequences of laziness

key_verses.text: Go to the ant, O sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise.
Without having any chief, she prepares her bread in summer and gathers her food in harvest.
A slack hand causes poverty, but the hand of the diligent makes rich.
He who gathers in summer is a prudent son, but he who sleeps in harvest is a son who brings shame.
Like vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes, so is the sluggard to those who send him.

clusters.name: Laziness and Poverty
clusters.description: Warnings about the inevitable consequences of idleness and neglect

key_verses.text: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest.
And poverty will come upon you like a robber, and want like an armed man.

clusters.name: Debt and Financial Risk
clusters.description: Warnings about co-signing, pledges, and the snare of debt commitments

key_verses.text: My son, if you have put up security for your neighbor, have given your pledge for a stranger...
If you are snared in the words of your mouth, caught in the words of your mouth.
Do this then, my son, and save yourself; humble yourself, and plead urgently with your neighbor.
Save yourself like a gazelle from the hand of the hunter, like a bird from the hand of the fowler.
He who puts up security for a stranger will surely suffer harm, but he who hates striking hands in pledge is secure.
Do not say to your neighbor, 'Go, and come again, tomorrow I will give it'—when you have it with you.

clusters.name: Generosity and Giving
clusters.description: The paradox of generosity—giving leads to abundance, withholding leads to want

key_verses.text: Do not withhold good from those to whom it is due, when it is in your power to do it.
One gives freely, yet grows all the richer; another withholds what he should give, and only suffers want.
Whoever brings blessing will be enriched, and he who waters will himself be watered.
The people curse him who holds back grain, but a blessing is on the head of him who sells it.

clusters.name: Stewardship and Tithing
clusters.description: Honoring God with the firstfruits and receiving abundance in return

key_verses.text: Honor the Lord with your wealth and with the firstfruits of all your produce.
Then your barns will be filled with plenty, and your vats will be bursting with wine.

clusters.name: Wisdom's True Value
clusters.description: Wisdom surpasses silver, gold, and jewels in worth and provides enduring wealth

key_verses.text: Blessed is the one who finds wisdom, and the one who gets understanding.
For the gain from her is better than gain from silver and her profit better than gold.
She is more precious than jewels, and nothing you desire can compare with her.
The beginning of wisdom is this: Get wisdom, and whatever you get, get insight.
Take my instruction instead of silver, and knowledge rather than choice gold.
For wisdom is better than jewels, and all that you may desire cannot compare with her.
Riches and honor are with me, enduring wealth and righteousness.
My fruit is better than gold, even fine gold, and my yield than choice silver.
Granting an inheritance to those who love me, and filling their treasuries.

clusters.name: Integrity and Honesty
clusters.description: The importance of honest business practices and just weights

key_verses.text: Treasures gained by wickedness do not profit, but righteousness delivers from death.
A false balance is an abomination to the Lord, but a just weight is his delight.
Riches do not profit in the day of wrath, but righteousness delivers from death.
The wage of the righteous leads to life, the gain of the wicked to sin.

clusters.name: Wealth, Poverty and Social Impact
clusters.description: The relationship between wealth and security, poverty and ruin, and the impact of character

key_verses.text: The Lord does not let the righteous go hungry, but he thwarts the craving of the wicked.
A rich man's wealth is his strong city; the poverty of the poor is their ruin.
The blessing of the Lord makes rich, and he adds no sorrow with it.
A gracious woman gets honor, and violent men get riches.
People do not despise a thief if he steals to satisfy his appetite when he is hungry. Yet if he is caught, he will pay sevenfold; he will give all the goods of his house.
Such are the ways of everyone who is greedy for unjust gain; it takes away the life of its possessors.

clusters.name: Fidelity and Resource Management
clusters.description: Guarding against wasting resources and the consequences of unfaithfulness

key_verses.text: Lest strangers take their fill of your strength, and your labors go to the house of a foreigner.
